rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to observe all 10 compounds while preserving retention of weakly retained components. The remaining high-organic hold allows late compounds to elute, and the peak-spacing pattern will guide subsequent optimization.

Halve the gradient duration to reduce the time penalty while testing whether the current resolution margin withstands compression. Keep the starting composition and temperature fixed to isolate the gradient-slope effect.

A modestly shallower gradient should improve the compressed central cluster while keeping the last peak close to the zero-time-penalty region. This brackets the resolution–speed tradeoff before adjusting temperature for selectivity.

Increase the gradient duration another two minutes to improve the sole unresolved pair while testing the boundary of the zero-time-penalty region. The other pairs retain sufficient resolution, making this a focused refinement of the current best method.

Raise temperature by 5 °C to test whether altered selectivity resolves the remaining critical pair without lengthening the gradient. Faster elution may also create room for a shallower gradient if further resolution is needed.

The critical pair converged as temperature increased, suggesting an elution-order crossover; 55 °C tests whether it separates again beyond that crossover. The surrounding gaps appear large enough to accommodate this selectivity shift while retaining zero time penalty.

Slightly steepen the gradient at 55 °C: after the apparent elution-order crossover, this may widen the remaining critical gap rather than compress it. The other pairs have resolution margin, and the shorter gradient should preserve zero time penalty.

Test a slightly shallower gradient between the slopes of injections 6 and 7, aiming to retain the maximum CRF while improving the smaller gap preceding the central cluster. The final peak should remain comfortably within the zero-time-penalty region.

The maximum score is already achieved; this explores an alternative with potentially greater resolution margin. Higher temperature should widen the crossover pair, while the shallower gradient may protect the earlier close pair without pushing the last peak beyond 10 minutes.

Return to 55 °C and test a higher starting organic fraction to probe selectivity beyond gradient slope alone. This may provide another maximum-score method with shorter retention, though both close pairs will need checking.

Lengthen the gradient slightly to raise the earlier critical pair above 1.5 while retaining the selectivity benefit of the higher starting organic fraction. The later critical pair has some margin, and the final peak should remain within the zero-time-penalty region.
Test an intermediate gradient slope between injections 10 and 11 to balance the two critical gaps. This could retain CRF 1.000 with a shorter last-peak time than injection 11.

Reduce the endpoint another grid step to improve the earlier critical gap while keeping the later gap above 1.5. This slope lies near the successful injection 11 and should preserve zero time penalty.

Lengthen the gradient to improve the sole pair below 1.5 while retaining the later pair’s resolution margin. The last peak is expected to remain below 10 minutes, potentially yielding another maximum-score method with improved minimum resolution.

Test a slope between injections 14 and 15 to shorten retention while aiming to keep both critical resolutions above 1.5. The maximum CRF is already established; this probes a faster alternative to injection 15 with useful resolution margin.

Test whether injection 11 retains maximum CRF with a two-minute longer gradient, mapping the range of acceptable slopes. The earlier critical gap should widen, while the later gap is predicted to remain just above 1.5 and the last peak below 10 minutes.

Reduce the endpoint to give a slope close to injection 15, which achieved maximum CRF with the largest observed minimum resolution. This tests an alternative expected to keep both critical gaps near 1.7 and the last peak below 10 minutes.

Return to the successful 55 °C regime and test a slope between injections 11 and 17, both of which achieved maximum CRF. This should preserve full resolution and zero time penalty while extending the range of demonstrated maximum-score methods.
Test a gradient slope between injections 16 and 15, aiming to retain maximum CRF with both critical resolutions above 1.5. The last peak should elute near 9.1 minutes, preserving zero time penalty.

Preserve the successful gradient slope while lowering the endpoint and shortening the programmed gradient again. Since all peaks previously eluted before this gradient would end at the outlet, the method should retain CRF 1.000.
